# Bug hunt

<!-- generated by scripts/project_map/build.py from scripts/mutants.yaml and docs/assets/generated/bug_hunt.json (scripts/bug_hunt.py) -- do not edit this file -->

A testbench is only as good as the bugs it catches. The RTL of the router carries **10 deliberate bugs**, each behind a `` `define `` (`BUG_*` in `yapp_project/rtl`, listed in `scripts/mutants.yaml`): compile the design with one of them and the regression must fail. `make bug-hunt` (`scripts/bug_hunt.py`) compiles the design once per bug, runs every test of the project on it and records which tests catch it; the `bughunt` workflow does the same in CI and goes red when a bug survives. This page is that record.

!!! tip "For the mentor"
    Give a student a build with one bug (`cd yapp_project/tb && make sim TEST=... DEFINES=BUG_...`) and the log and waves of a failing test: finding *where* the design is wrong from *what* the testbench reports is the exercise. The sections below are the answers.
